words: لَوْ بَسَطَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ لَبَغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains withholding abundant provision by the transgression it would cause among people.
rows.anchor: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض

words: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prevented signs are requested miracles, not signs God initially sends to establish the messengers’ truth.
rows.anchor: أي آيات الاقتراح لا الآيات الدالة على صدق الرسل التي تأتي منه سبحانه ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A visibly sent angel would bring immediate punishment if rejected; a human messenger allows contact, while an angel in human form would be dismissed as human.
rows.anchor: لو أنزل عليه الملك ثم عاينوه ولم يؤمنوا به لعوجلوا بالعقوبة جعل الرسول بشرا ليمكنهم التلقي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cites the prospect of humanity becoming one community as the impediment to granting unbelievers extravagant worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical non-Arabic Quran illustrates that an objection would prevent a form of revelation from achieving its purpose.
rows.anchor: ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reports the purposes and benefits built into creation and command, including the earth as a resting place, houses as shelter, and spouses for comfort.
rows.anchor: إخباره عن الحكم والغايات التني جعلها في خلقه وأمره

words: وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine discourse uses both exhaustive elaboration and concise generalization; the cited poetic line illustrates the latter.
rows.anchor: وكما يقصدون البسط والاستيفاء يقصدون الإجمال والإيجاز كما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of a lofty garden with near clusters sets height against nearness as antithesis.
rows.anchor: في جنة عالية قطوفها دانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised couches and placed cups likewise form an antithetical pairing.
rows.anchor: فيها سرر مرفوعة وأكواب موضوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day, opposites, are matched with rest and activity; “seeking His bounty” indirectly names purposeful motion and adds rhetorical refinement.
rows.anchor: فذكر الليل والنهار وهما ضدان ثم قابلهما بضدين وهما الحركة والسكون على الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording favors seeking bounty over simply saying movement because such activity serves benefit, uses strength and sound judgment, and directs the traveler toward an aim.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن لفظ الحركة إلى لفظ ابتغاء الفضل لكون الحركة تكون للمصلحة دون المفسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers’ “our Lord knows” means “our Lord knows we are truthful,” an implicit semantic opposite to the people’s accusation that they lie.
rows.anchor: معناه ربنا يعلم إنا لصادقون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says “building” denotes a raised structure, so it is paired antithetically with the earth as a bed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي في الحجة لما كان البناء رفعا للمبنى قوبل بالفراش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drowning followed by entry into fire makes an understated antithesis by joining water’s characteristic with fire.
rows.anchor: لأن الغرق من صفات الماء فكأنه جمع بين الماء في النار والنار

rows.speaker: ابن منقذ
rows.claim: Ibn Munqidh calls the drowning-and-fire example the Quran’s most hidden antithesis.
rows.anchor: ابن منقذ 2 وهي أخفى مطابقة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire produced from a green tree juxtaposes green with fire’s red and also exhibits decorative color contrast.
rows.anchor: قلت ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ من الشجر الأخضر نارا ﴾ 3

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retribution entails killing, yet that killing becomes a cause of life, creating a subtle antithesis.
rows.anchor: لأن معنى القصاص القتل فصار القتل سبب الحياة

rows.speaker: ابن المعتز
rows.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz calls the retribution-and-life pairing one of the most graceful and subtle antitheses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المعتز 5 وهذا من أملح الطباق وأخفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Shadow” implies daytime, and when paired with blackness it indirectly evokes the contrast with white.
rows.anchor: لأن ظل لا تستعمل إلا نهارا فإذا لمح مع ذكر السواد كأنه طباق يذكر البياض مع السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker’s call to salvation is directly opposed to the people’s call to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of “made” for Adam’s mate in al-Aʿraf and “created” in al-Nisa shows that the two verbs can be near-synonyms.
rows.anchor: فهو يدل على انهما قد يستعملان استعمال المترادفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth sense of jaʿala is to transform something from one state into another; it takes two objects, as in physical transformations.
rows.anchor: الرابع بمعنى النقل من حال إلى حال والتصيير فيتعدى إلى مفعولين اما حسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same two-object transformation sense can be mental, or concern changing a thing into a condition or role, as with gods, messengers, safety, and night as clothing.
rows.anchor: وإما عقلا مثل ﴿ أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples make the source and destination of transformation explicit; in “day a livelihood,” maʿāsh may mean a time noun or a verbal noun meaning livelihood.
rows.anchor: في قوله ﴿ وجعلنا النهار معاشا ﴾ 15 اسم زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making Mary and her son a sign means rendering them a sign: Jesus was created from her without a father, making them a proof for the worlds.
rows.anchor: ومعناه صيرناه لان مريم انما صارت مع ولدها عليه السلام لما خلق من جسدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase cannot mean creating both then, since Mary already existed; making an existing being exist while it remains is impossible.
rows.anchor: ومحال انه يريد خلقناهما لان مريم لم تخلق في حين خلق ولدها بل كانت موجوده قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Made it an Arabic Quran” is an extended use meaning that God rendered it recitable in Arabic; earlier scriptures contained its meanings in Hebrew or Syriac.
rows.anchor: أي صيرناه يقرا بلسان عربي لان غير القرآن ماهو عبري وسرياني

rows.speaker: من أجاز القراءة بالفارسية
rows.claim: Those permitting recitation in Persian argue that earlier scriptures held Quranic meanings rather than its Arabic wording, and Persian can convey those meanings.
rows.anchor: وبهذا احتج من أجاز القراءة بالفارسية قال لأنه ليس في زبر الأولين من القرآن إلا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “when you disperse from Arafat,” the omitted object is yourselves.
rows.anchor: فإذا أفضتم من عرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “taste because you forgot the meeting of this day,” the omitted object is the punishment.
rows.anchor: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Abraham’s prayer, “I settled some of my progeny,” an understood object is people or a group.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ إني أسكنت من ذريتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “ask your Lord to bring forth for us,” the omitted object is “something.”
rows.anchor: فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the earth being changed into another earth and the heavens, “other” is understood before “the heavens.”
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات ﴾ 6 أي غير السموات

words: قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here duʿāʾ means naming: call Him Allah or al-Rahman; otherwise one-object invocation would imply either shirk or naming the same deity twice.
rows.anchor: على أن الدعاء بمعنى التسمية التي تتعدى إلى مفعولين أي سموه الله أو سموه الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted object can show contempt; “God has decreed that I and My messengers will prevail” leaves the disbelievers unnamed.
rows.anchor: ومنها قصد الاحتقار كقوله ﴿ كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omission, especially under negation, can generalize the object: signs and warnings avail no unbelieving people, and the people were not believers at all.
rows.anchor: ومنها قصد التعميم ولا سيما إذا كان في حيز النفي

words: فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًۭا وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Objects are often omitted at verse endings, including “while you know” and “while you recite the Book”; omission asserts the verb for its subject without restricting its object.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما يعترى الحذف في رءوس الآى نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God invites everyone to the abode of peace because the invitation is universal, while guidance is particular.
rows.anchor: أي كل أحد لأن الدعوة عامة والهداية خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measure and weigh take two objects, one introduced by li; the second is omitted to generalize what the defrauders withhold.
rows.anchor: والتقدير كالوا ووزنوا لهم وحذف المفعول الثاني لقصد التعميم

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari says the pronoun after li is an accusative object; he rejects the mistaken analysis that it is a subject pronoun emphasizing the plural verb.
rows.anchor: وقرره ابن الشجري في أماليه قال وأخطأ بعض المتأولين حيث زعم أن هم ضمير مرفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth sense of jaʿala is to believe or consider something so, as when unbelievers assign partners to God or regard angels as female.
rows.anchor: الخامس بمعنى الإعتقاد كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “made the angels female” is transformation in the mind: unbelievers’ belief renders them female in their mental representation, though not in reality.
rows.anchor: ووجه النقل فيه هو إن الملائكة في نفس الامر ليسوا إناثا فهؤلاء الكفار نقلوهم باعتقادهم

rows.speaker: منهم
rows.claim: Some take “make rivals for God” to mean naming idols as rivals, while also implying belief, since the unbelievers would not name them so without believing it.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعلها بمعنى التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the Quran into parts means naming and dividing it, calling some of it poetry, magic, and tales of the ancients.
rows.anchor: أي سموه وجزءوه أجزاء فجعلوا بعضه شعرا وبعضه سحرا وبعضه أساطير الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you made the watering of pilgrims equal to faith?” means “have you considered this like that?”
rows.anchor: أي اعتقدتم هذا مثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison asks that the states of believers and corrupters not be made alike: the transformation concerns their condition.
rows.anchor: فالنقل والتصيير راجعان إلى الحال أي لاتجعل حال هؤلاء مثل حال هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “or have they made partners for God who create like His creation,” jaʿala means to believe in partners.
rows.anchor: أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth sense is to judge or declare something about something, whether truthfully, as in making Moses one of the messengers, or falsely, as in assigning God a share of crops.
rows.anchor: السادس بمعنى الحكم بالشئ على الشئ يكون في الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿala can mean to prescribe or impose, as with the direction of prayer and the prohibited designations of certain livestock.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى أوجب كقوله تعالى ﴿ وما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You were upon it” means “you are upon it,” just as “you were the best community” means “you are.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى كنت عليها أي انت عليها كقوله

rows.speaker: أبو الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi gives a seventh sense, “to place,” taking two objects: one direct and one with a preposition, as in placing possessions one over another.
rows.anchor: ذكره الفارسي بمعنى القى فيتعدى لمفعولين احدهما بنفسه والآخر بحرف الجر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows a conjunctive waw, which the author rejects because it makes God tell the Prophet to leave both Him and the created person; the sense is to leave God alone with them.
rows.anchor: أجاز أبو البقاء كون الواو عاطفة وهو فاسد لأنه يلزم فيه إن يكون الله تعالى أمر نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended idiom is “leave me to deal with them,” like leaving a she-camel with her foal to suckle.
rows.anchor: فتعين إن يكون المراد خل بيني وبينهم وهو وارد مع كقولك لو تركت الناقة وفصيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resumptive waw introduces an independent clause, not dependent in meaning or sharing a grammatical slot; it may introduce nominal or verbal clauses and prevents mistaking a clause for a single coordinated word.
rows.anchor: واو الاستثناء وتسمى واو القطع والابتداء وهي التي يكون بعدها جملة غير متعلقة بما قبلها في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial waw enters a nominal clause and can replace a pronoun referring back to the clause’s subject.
rows.anchor: واو الحال الداخلة على الجملة الاسمية وهي عندهم مغنية عن ضمير صاحبها

words: فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًۭا وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resumptive coordination and circumstantial waw occur together, as in “while you know,” “while you recite the Book,” and the other cited clauses.
rows.anchor: وقد يجتمعان نحو ﴿ فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون ﴾

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says he asked for fourteen years who the emigrant in the verse was, then learned it was Damra ibn al-ʿAys, a sick, vulnerable Meccan who left after the hijra command and died at Tanʿim.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة أقمت أربع عشرة سنة أسال عنه حتى عرفته هو ضمرة بن العيص

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said the verse concerns Ali, who gave one of four dirhams by day, one by night, one secretly, and one openly.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت في على كان معه أربع دوانق فتصدق بواحد بالنهار وآخر باليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said the hunting-animal verse concerns ʿAdi ibn Hatim, whose five dogs had proper names.
rows.anchor: كان له كلاب [ خمسة ] قد سماها [ بأسماء ] أعلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description “people of virtue” honors without naming its referent; it means Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: قوله ﴿ ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم ﴾ والمراد الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The one who brought the truth” refers to Muhammad, and “confirmed it” refers to Abu Bakr; the wording also includes every person who confirms the truth.
rows.anchor: تعظيمه بالوصف الكامل دون الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deficient description “your enemy” demeans by indirect reference and means al-ʿAsi ibn Waʾil.
rows.anchor: والمراد فيها العاصى بن وائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling someone “a transgressor” rather than naming him refers to al-Walid ibn ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt.
rows.anchor: والمراد الوليد بن عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab is named to alert the audience that his fate is the Fire of flame, echoing his name.
rows.anchor: فذكره هنالك للتنبيه على أن ما له للنار ذات اللهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel is used instead of Jacob when addressing the Israelites to recall God and their ancestors’ religion; the name is interpreted as connected to God.
rows.anchor: سموا بالاسم الذى فيه تذكرة بالله فإن إسرائيل اسم مضاف إلى الله سبحانه فى التأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When addressing converts called sons of Abdullah, the Prophet used their father’s name to urge the servitude it implies; the source uses this as a parallel.
rows.anchor: يحرضهم بذلك على ما يقتضيه اسمه من العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob is named in the glad tidings to Abraham because this gift followed another; Yaʿqub’s Arabic form also echoes succession and what comes after.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر موهبته لإبراهيم وتبشيره به قال يعقوب وكان أولى من إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted alif in bism signals the name’s elevated, unique rank and its connection to God, whose name gathers all names; the spelling also evokes manifestation and hiddenness.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على علوه فى أول رتبة الأسماء وانفراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted alif in al-Rahman reflects that people know mercy’s effects but entrust knowledge of its full reality to God.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حذفت الألف قبل النون من اسمه الرحمن حيث وقع بيانا لأنا نعلم حقائق تفصيل رحمته

rows.speaker: علماء الظاهر
rows.claim: The outward scholars explain the omission as abbreviation from frequent use: the alif of ism is dropped only when appended to Allah and preceded by ba according to the majority.
rows.anchor: وعلماء الظاهر يقولون للاختصار وكثرة الاستعمال وهو من خصائص الجلالة الشريفة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi does not require the preceding ba and permits deletion in forms such as bism al-malik; the majority requires ba.
rows.anchor: ولم يشترط الكسائى الثانى فجوز حذفها كما تحذف فى بسم الملك والجمهور على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif is also omitted from some active-participle forms such as qadara and ʿalima because it lies inside the word.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حذف الألف فى كثير من أسماء الفاعلين مثل قدر وعلم وذلك أن هذه الألف فى وسط الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In sound and broken plurals, a surplus alif is deleted when the detailed meaning is latent and retained when it is manifest.
rows.anchor: فإنها كلها وردت لمعنى مفصل يشتمل عليه معنى تلك اللفظة فتحذف حيث يبطن التفصيل وتثبت حيث يظهر

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reports agreement to omit alif in common foreign names such as Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Harun, and Luqman; other foreign names retain it when uncommon.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو اتفقوا على حذف الألف من الأعلام الأعجمية المستعملة كإبرهيم وأسمعيل واسحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif is also deleted in Sulayman, Salih, and Malik because they are frequently used, while uncommon foreign names such as Talut, Jalut, Yaʾjuj, and Maʾjuj keep it.
rows.anchor: وأما حذفها من سليمن وصلح وملك وليست بأعجمية فلكثرة الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about creation requires the days to have been created after some of the things mentioned in the hadith.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن تأخر خلق الأيام عن بعض الأشياء المذكورة في الخبر لازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith appears to contradict this by saying God created soil on Saturday, the first created item it mentions, before the days could have been created.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت الحديث كالمصرح بخلافه فإنه قال خلق الله التربة يوم السبت حين خلق البرية

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari resolves the difficulty by saying God named the days first, then assigned each a duration; soil was created during Saturday’s assigned span, before Saturday itself was created.
rows.anchor: قد نبه الطبري على جواب ذلك بما حاصله أن الله تعالى سمى أسماء الأيام قبل خلق التربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although contrary to the apparent wording, al-Tabari’s account is required by the evidence; the report describes estimated rather than actual time.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن الزمان قسمان تحقيقي وتقديري والمذكور في الحديث التقديري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic references to two easts and two wests, the east and west of the earth, and then plural easts illustrate the range of paired and plural forms.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ رب المشرقين ورب المغربين ﴾ 1 ﴿ مشارق الأرض ومغاربها ﴾ 2

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several explanations account for mentioning death before life: the order subdues creatures, human life is like death and leads back to death, and life follows death.
rows.anchor: منها أن فيه قهرا للخلق والمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If death means nonexistence, it preceded life because humans were dead before receiving the spirit, as “you were dead, then He gave you life” indicates.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن الموت تقدم في الوجود إذ الإنسان قبل نفخ الروح فيه كان ميتا لعدم الروح

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers define death as the absence of life in something that is by nature capable of living.
rows.anchor: فقالت الفلاسفة الموت عدم الحياة عما من شأنه أن يكون حيا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority holds that death is an existent entity opposed to life, citing God’s creation of death and life and the hadith in which death appears as a ram and is slaughtered.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنه أمر وجودي يضاد الحياة محتجين بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can be answered by taking “created” to mean decreed, which does not require the decreed thing to exist; the slaughter report is a parable of death ending and permanence beginning.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عن الآية بان الخلق بمعنى التقدير ولا يجب في المقدر أن يكون وجوديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Gabriel is coordinated with God, the verse is not an instance of this category; even if coordinated with the messengers, the likely referents are human messengers, distinct from the angels.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فيجوز ان يكون جبريل معطوفا على لفظ الجلالة فلا تكون الآية من هذا النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is tied to revelation, which gives life to hearts, and Michael to provision, which gives life to bodies; the Jews’ explicit hostility to them occasioned the verse.
rows.anchor: انه سبحانه وتعالى خصهما بالحياة فجبريل بالوحي الذي هو حياة القلوب وميكائيل بالرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is mentioned before Michael because life of the heart is greater than life of the body.
rows.anchor: أن حياة القلوب أعظم من حياة الأبدان ومن ثم قيل

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو الطيب الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib al-Tabari argues that the indefinite “fruit” in an affirmative context is general, so pomegranate can be mentioned after it as a particular.
rows.anchor: كما ذكره القاضي أبو الطيب الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a broader account: “general” and “particular” here are not technical legal categories, but any first item encompassing a later one.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنه ليس المراد بالخاص والعام هاهنا المصطلح عليه في الأصول

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Because conjunction implies difference, Abu Hanifa rules that someone who swore off fruit does not break the oath by eating a pomegranate.
rows.anchor: ولما لمح أبو حنيفة معنى العطف وهو المغايرة لم يحنث الحالف على أكل الفاكهة بأكل الرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling people to good already includes enjoining good and forbidding wrong, so the latter are named as parts of the former.
rows.anchor: إذ الأمر والنهي من جملة الدعاء إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly mentioning belief in what was revealed to Muhammad honors the Prophet and his revelation, since faith is incomplete without it.
rows.anchor: والقصد تفضيل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما نزل عليه إذ لايتم الإيمان إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about benefits and drinks is another example in the discussion of coordinated general and particular items.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although idolaters are already included among people, naming them separately emphasizes their greater eagerness for life because they disbelieve in resurrection.
rows.anchor: أن حرصهم على الحياة اشد لانهم كانوا لا يؤمنون بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some object to the majority’s feminine “the angels called” because it echoes pagan claims that angels are women; others object to a reading without the feminine marker because angels are plural. Both objections are unsound: both readings are mutawatir and neither should be rejected.
rows.anchor: والقراءتان متواترتان فلا ينبغى أن ترد إحداهما البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah, “Gabriel called to him,” supports taking “the angels” to refer to one angel.
rows.anchor: فناداه جبريل / ما يؤيد أن الملائكة مراد به الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What I worship” refers to the worshipped object in general: opponents thought they worshipped God but did not know Him, so Muhammad says they do not worship his object of worship.
rows.anchor: فهي على بابها لأنها واقعة على معبوده عليه السلام على الإطلاق لأن الكفار كانوا يظنون انهم يعبدون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ambiguous “what” also suits opponents intent on contradicting him whatever his deity, and matches their nonrational object of worship and the passage’s parallel phrasing.
rows.anchor: كانوا يحسدونه ويقصدون مخالفته كائنا من كان معبوده فلا يصح في اللفظ إلا لفظة ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future form for the Prophet signals protection from deviation; the present form for opponents suggests that their worship follows changeable desires and objects.
rows.anchor: وكرر الفعل على بنية المستقبل حيث أخبر عن نفسه إيماء إلى عصمة الله له عن الزيغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is declarative or relative before laysa, lam, or la, and after illa, as in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: إذا جاءت قبل ليس أو لم أو لا أو بعد إلا فإنها تكون خبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma after a preposition is generally declarative, except after the comparative kaf; after ba it may instead be a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إذا جاءت بعد حرف الجر نحو ربما وعما وفيما ونظائرهاإلا بعد كاف التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ba, ma can function as a verbal noun, as in “because of what they used to do” and related phrases.
rows.anchor: وربما كانت مصدرا بعد الباء نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between verbs of knowing, awareness, or looking, ma may be either declarative or interrogative; the source gives examples of both readings.
rows.anchor: وإن وقعت بين فعلين سابقهما علم أو دراية أو نظر جاز فيها الخبر والاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conditional ma takes the front of the clause and is governed by the following verb, as in the cited conditions about abrogation and good deeds.
rows.anchor: الثاني الشرطية ولها صدر الكلام ويعمل فيها ما بعدها من الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general exception about lawful cattle is clarified by another verse listing forbidden carrion, blood, pork, and other foods.
rows.anchor: فهذا الاستثناء مجمل بينه فى آية أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspecified test involving game is clarified by the prohibition on hunting while in ihram.
rows.anchor: فهذا الابتلاء مجمل لا يعلم أحد فى الحل أم فى الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction that the defeated will later prevail is presented alongside a verse identifying the Messenger’s religion of truth as divinely sent.
rows.anchor: وهذا المجمل بينه فى آية أخرى

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars explain the covenant by the conditions in 5:12: if Israel fulfills its obligations, God fulfills His promise to forgive their sins.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء بيان هذا العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ claim that Muhammad is no messenger is answered by the oath and declaration that he is among the messengers.
rows.anchor: يس والقرآن الحكيم إنك لمن المرسلين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One answer to the plea to remove punishment is that, even if shown mercy and relieved, they would persist blindly in transgression.
rows.anchor: ولو رحمناهم وكشفنا ما بهم من ضر للجوا في طغيانهم يعمهون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the later promise “We are removing the punishment” answers the plea, with an implied condition: if relief comes, they will relapse.
rows.anchor: والتقدير إن كشفنا العذاب تعودوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand to reveal the Quran to a great man from one of the two towns is answered by saying that God creates and chooses as He wills.
rows.anchor: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people ask who al-Rahman is, the answer is that the Merciful taught the Quran.
rows.anchor: بيانه ﴿ الرحمن علم القرآن ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boast that the disbelievers could produce a comparable text is answered by the challenge for humans and jinn together to produce its like.
rows.anchor: لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elites’ order to persist patiently with their gods is answered that if they persist, the Fire will be their home.
rows.anchor: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم
